    The Hom criterion for two-term presilting complexes #

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.exists_lift_of_exact {R : Type u} [Ring R] [IsNoetherianRing R] {X A B C : FGModuleCat R} [Module.Projective R ↑X] {f : A ⟶ B} {g : B ⟶ C} (hfg : CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f g = 0) (h : { X₁ := A, X₂ := B, X₃ := C, f := f, g := g, zero := hfg }.Exact) (v : X ⟶ B) (hv : CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp v g = 0) :
    ∃ (a : X ⟶ A), CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp a f = v

    A map from a projective into the middle term of an exact pair lifts along the first map if its composite with the second map is zero.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.surjective_boundary_iff_surjective_precompose {R : Type u} [Ring R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (P Q : TwoTerm R) :
    Function.Surjective ⇑(P.homotopyBoundary Q) ↔ Function.Surjective ⇑(P.precompose (CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel Q.differential))

    For two projective differentials, the degree-one homotopy boundary is surjective exactly when precomposition into the second cokernel is surjective.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.surjective_precompose_iff_no_hom_nakayamaKernel {R : Type u} [Ring R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (k : Type u) [Field k] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] (P : TwoTerm R) (M : FGModuleCat R) :
    Function.Surjective ⇑(P.precompose M) ↔ Subsingleton (M ⟶ nakayamaKernel k P)

    The Nakayama kernel represents the obstruction to surjectivity on Hom.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.isPresilting_iff_no_hom_nakayamaKernel {R : Type u} [Ring R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (k : Type u) [Field k] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] (P : TwoTerm R) :
    P.IsPresilting ↔ Subsingleton (CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel P.differential ⟶ nakayamaKernel k P)

    A two-term projective complex is presilting precisely when the Hom from its cokernel to its Nakayama kernel vanishes.
